title: post-loop-accelerator-handoff-noemi-ramos
content:
Candidate: Jordan Park (final interview loop)
Interviewer: Noemi Ramos (serving runtime)
Context: spent ~1.5h technical deep dive + 30m behavioral. Candidate came through referrals, strong ML infra resume (previously at Nebula ML serving). Goal of this note: capture quick heuristics for leveling, questions to follow up, and a short ramp sketch to attach to the hiring packet.

Quick ratings (1-5):
- System design / architecture: 4
- Low-level performance intuition (memory, batching): 4
- Software engineering (readability, testing, shipping): 3
- Debugging / oncall instincts: 5
- Communication and cross-team collaboration: 4

Top signals (why I leaned positive):
- Demonstrated concrete heuristics for balancing batch size vs latency: used request distribution percentiles and KV cache hit-rate tradeoffs. Gave a crisp example of switching between prefix caching and per-request caching for conversational workloads.
- Strong incident story: led a rollback during a P0 due to a subtle cache invalidation bug. Orchestrated a postmortem, wrote the mitigation (short-term config guard + long-term test) — shows ownership.
- Familiarity with quantization caveats and quantization-aware batching; could name failure modes we've seen in the field (out-of-distribution token misalignment causing tokenization edge cases).

Red flags / open concerns:
- Tests and CI discipline seemed thinner — their unit/e2e testing examples were ad-hoc scripts rather than integrated pipelines. Would expect stronger test automation for a senior hire owning critical runtime paths.
- Some answers on kernel selection felt higher-level; when pushed on concrete profiling steps (how to measure L2 vs L3 cache stalls vs kernel flops) they sketched approaches but didn't have a reproducible profile pipeline ready. Could be coaching gap.

Concrete anecdotes to include in feedback:
- When asked about degrading gracefully under load, Jordan sketched 3-tier fallback: (1) degrade to 8-bit quantized model, (2) route to cheaper model variant in another region, (3) return cached stub replies for low-value queries. They actually enumerated metrics to monitor for each step (95th token latency, cache hit delta, cost per 1k tokens) which was helpful.
- During the incident story they specifically mentioned adding a feature flag check that prevented a regression from hitting customers again — pragmatic and safety-oriented.

Recommended follow-ups / probing (for a second, short conversation or panel):
- Ask them to walk through a concrete profile run: given a 16GB GPU and a 1.5k sequence workload, what exact steps would they run, which profilers, and what numbers would indicate kernel mismatch? (probe for reproducible measurement steps).
- Give a small design exercise: how would you modify batching to prioritize 99th percentile latency for a real-time chat product while keeping cost per 1k tokens within 10% of baseline? (look for concrete knobs and monitoring thresholds).
- Request an example PR or test from their repo that shows an automated regression test for a performance-sensitive change.

Suggested leveling and role fit:
- Level: Senior Engineer (IC4) leaning toward Senior+ (IC5) depending on test automation and reproducible profiling evidence.
- Good fit for: runtime performance, oncall rotation, incident leads, model-variant fallback policy work. Could own a cross-team initiative (routing and cache policy).

Ramp sketch (30/60/90 days) — include in packet if hired:
- 30d: onboard to core runtime, reproduce one small perf test locally (baseline and a 5% improvement PR), shadow oncall and run 1 postmortem review.
- 60d: deliver a safe default fallback policy (canary + config guard) for one model family, include tests and dashboards.
- 90d: lead a small project to reduce p99 latency for a target workload by 10% (ownership of measurement, implementation, rollout).

Notes to self (private):
- Keep question bank focused on reproducibility. Candidate's operational instincts are strong; need to ensure they can convert intuition into repeatable pipelines.
- If laddering to IC5, require concrete examples of shipping cross-team infra and mentoring/leadership signals.

Action items (for hiring packet):
- Attach a one-paragraph leveling justification and the 30/60/90 sketch.
- Ask hiring manager to request 1 PR or test artifact from candidate.
- If panel agrees, shortlist for offer but include a small pre-start checklist item: pair with runtime infra for 2hrs to demonstrate profiling pipeline.

Miscellaneous:
- Candidate timezone: PST.
- Compensation expectation: ~market for Senior (disclosed during loop).
- Cultural fit: pragmatic, non-academic; comfortable shipping production tradeoffs.

End of note.
summary: Captured rapid debrief and leveling heuristics for Jordan Park — strong on incident response and runtime fallbacks, needs reproducible profiling/tests to justify IC5. Recommended Senior hire with follow-up artifact request.
